issues.description: `cad sweep` with a negative range start (-45:45:15) fails with 'arguments are required: values' because argparse reads it as a flag. A comma list with negatives fails too. It only works with `--` after the options, e.g. `cad sweep shoulder --min 0.5 -- -45:45:15`. The help doesn't mention this, and the error message is misleading.

`cad set` persists poses into params.toml, so a checking pose can be left in the deliverable. I had to reset every parameter to 0 by hand. After the reset, params.toml holds explicit zeros rather than being absent.

`extrude(..., plane='XZ', offset=d)` puts the sketch at Y=-d and positive distances go toward -Y. The docs explain this, but it is easy to get wrong. I had to confirm the Y slabs with `cad measure --bbox` and `--holes`.
Joint docs say to use `part.faces("hinge.wall")` for a hole axis, but a hole made with cylinder(op=cut) exposes `<name>.side`, not `.wall` (UNKNOWN_REFERENCE; the hint did list .side).

`cad sweep PARAM -45:45:15` fails because the negative start is parsed as an option; `--` must come after the other flags (`cad sweep p --min 0.5 -- -45:45:15`). The error only said 'values required'.

The XZ-plane extrude offset/sign convention (offset=-y0, negative distance toward +Y) is easy to get wrong. A first-pass turret post, a cylinder, overlapped the lower arm because I forgot its Y extent.

`cad sweep PARAM -45:45:15` (and quoted comma lists starting with a minus) fail with 'the following arguments are required: values' because argparse reads the negative start as an option. Ranges with negative values (every symmetric joint range) can't be swept directly.
Because of the sweep issue I had to `cad set <joint> <value>` and run `cad clearance` per extreme pose, then reset to 0.

Joint positive direction follows the right-hand rule about the auto-picked +Y axis, so the elbow went the wrong way (lowered the head). `cad joints` wording ('far end moves +Z (up)') caught it, but the docs don't say to check this or that direction='-y' is the usual fix for a Y-axis hinge.
`cad set` writes joint values to params.toml, so a verification pose persists into the deliverable unless reset to 0 afterwards.

suggestions.suggestion: Make `cad sweep` accept negative ranges directly, for example by using nargs handling or allowing `--values`.
Add a `cad set --reset` or `cad set --temp` so inspection poses don't persist in params.toml.
Let `cad clearance` and `cad sweep` print only violations, or the overall minimum, to keep output short.
Accept negative sweep ranges directly, or say in the error and help how to pass them.
Document hole face names (.side) in the joints section.
Let `cad joints` run with a hint when the parameter-driven pose is non-zero, and add a `cad render --pose yaw=90,...` option that doesn't alter the active revision.
Make sweep accept negative starts (e.g. `--` handling or `START..STOP`), and offer `cad sweep --all-limits` to test each joint's limits.
Offer a `cad sweep --all` that sweeps every joint to its limit extremes and checks clearances.
Warn in `cad set` output that the value was persisted to params.toml.
